label: tp-potential-probe
_why: DIAGNOSTIC (2026-10-18, overnight, user-authorised to try approaches): the extreme treaty-port book produced only 14 AI pairs wanting treaty ports by 1846, ALL against unrecognised or decentralised hosts, and 1-2 demands a run - so the engine computes the desire only where its own is_potential_treaty_port admits a state, and that seems to exclude recognised hosts. This one-month run logs, at the campaign start, for 10 takers x every coastal state of 31 hosts: is_potential_treaty_port, and the engine's own ai_treaty_port_value of that state for that taker (PMR_TPP lines in debug.log).

_arms.tpxp: {kind: config, config: config/mod_config.jex-dam4s-rs-x25-m10ac-dpriv-wm99-tpx-probe.json} - the extreme book + the probe log; + telemetry

_comparison: None: a census of what the engine admits.

_predictions.if recognition gates it: potential = no for every state of a recognised host (FRA, GBR, SPA, NET, BRZ, MEX, USA ...), yes for unrecognised hosts (CHI, JAP, PER, SIA, MOR ...)
_predictions.if rank gates it: potential follows the taker-vs-host rank, whatever recognition
_predictions.the value: positive (around 400+) wherever potential = yes and the parity cancel does not apply

_caveats: Launch ONLY through tools/testbed/launch_detached.ps1 CALLED DIRECTLY from the PowerShell tool (L30).
